transcript.en: A student's first neural network printed a loss of nan after three steps. She had copied the code exactly. The only change was a learning rate of ten instead of a tenth. Today: learning as minimising a loss, how gradient descent does it, and why the learning rate trips students up. Supervised learning picks the parameters that minimise the average loss on the training data. That average is the empirical risk. We hope it tracks the true risk on new data. Gradient descent starts somewhere and repeatedly steps against the gradient. Theta becomes theta minus eta times the gradient. Eta, the learning rate, sets the step size. Here is the loss after fifty steps on the same problem. A tiny rate barely moves. A good rate reaches nearly zero. A rate that is too big bounces higher and higher. Real datasets are large, so we estimate the gradient from a small random batch. Stochastic gradient descent is noisy, but each step is cheap, and the noise can even help escape flat regions. Students often think the gradient points to the minimum. It only points uphill, locally. Plot a one-parameter loss, let students take steps by hand, and they discover overshooting themselves. Quick check! The loss rises every step and then becomes nan. What is the most likely cause? The learning rate is too big. Each step overshoots the valley and lands higher up, until the numbers overflow. Divide it by ten and try again. In the app, open the gradient lab. Pick a starting point, change the learning rate, and watch the steps converge, crawl or explode. Your turn. The loss is theta squared, theta is three, and the learning rate is a tenth. Where is theta after one step? At two point four, because the gradient is six. Remember: learning minimises empirical risk, gradient descent steps downhill, and the learning rate decides whether it works. Try it in your next lecture: give each pair the loss theta squared and three learning rates. They take five steps by hand and plot them, before you show any code.

body.en:
Supervised learning chooses parameters θ that minimise the empirical risk R̂(θ) = (1/n) Σ ℓ(f_θ(xᵢ), yᵢ), the average loss on the training set, as a proxy for the true risk on new data (Goodfellow, Bengio and Courville, 2016, ch. 5). Gradient descent iterates θ ← θ − η∇R̂(θ). For a convex loss with a suitable step size it converges to the minimum; for neural networks it finds good, not global, minima.

The learning rate η dominates behaviour. Too small and progress crawls; too large and each step overshoots, so the loss grows and overflows to nan. For the loss θ², the update is θ ← (1 − 2η)θ, which diverges when η > 1, a calculation students can do by hand. Stochastic gradient descent estimates ∇R̂ from a mini-batch: each step is noisy but cheap, so it reaches good solutions faster in wall-clock time.

The classic misconception is that the gradient points to the minimum. It points in the direction of steepest local ascent and says nothing about where the minimum lies. Students who first take steps by hand on a one-parameter loss build an accurate picture of overshooting and convergence, which then transfers to the high-dimensional case.
body.ar:
يختار التعلّم الموجّه المعاملات θ التي تقلّل الخطر التجريبي R̂(θ) = ⁦(1/n)⁩ Σ ℓ(f_θ(xᵢ), yᵢ)، أي متوسط الخسارة على مجموعة التدريب، بديلًا عن الخطر الحقيقي على بيانات جديدة (Goodfellow وBengio وCourville، ٢٠١٦، الفصل ٥). ويكرّر الانحدار التدريجي التحديث θ ← θ − η∇R̂(θ). ومع خسارة محدّبة وحجم خطوة مناسب يتقارب إلى القيمة الصغرى، أما في الشبكات العصبية فيجد قيمًا صغرى جيدة لا عالمية.

ويهيمن معدّل التعلّم η على السلوك. فإن كان صغيرًا جدًا زحف التقدّم، وإن كان كبيرًا جدًا تجاوزت كل خطوة القاع، فتكبر الخسارة وتفيض إلى nan. وللخسارة θ² يكون التحديث θ ← (⁦1 − 2⁩η)θ، الذي يتباعد حين η ⁦> 1⁩، وهو حساب يستطيع الطلاب إجراءه يدويًا. ويقدّر الانحدار التدريجي العشوائي ∇R̂ من دفعة صغيرة: كل خطوة فيها ضوضاء لكنها رخيصة، فيصل إلى حلول جيدة أسرع في الزمن الفعلي.

والتصور الخاطئ الكلاسيكي أن التدرّج يشير إلى القيمة الصغرى. وهو في الحقيقة يشير إلى اتجاه أشد صعود محلي ولا يقول شيئًا عن موضع القاع. والطلاب الذين يأخذون خطوات يدويًا على خسارة بمعامل واحد يبنون صورة دقيقة لتجاوز القاع والتقارب، تنتقل بعد ذلك إلى الحالة متعددة الأبعاد.

transcript.en: I asked my class how a network with a million weights knows which ones to change. One student said: the framework does it. That answer is true. It is also the moment understanding stops. Today: how backpropagation computes every gradient in one backward pass, and how to make it concrete for students. A network is a chain of simple operations. The forward pass computes each value from inputs to loss. Backpropagation walks the same graph in reverse, applying the chain rule at each node. If the loss depends on a, and a depends on w, then the derivative of the loss with respect to w is the derivative with respect to a times the derivative of a with respect to w. Local derivatives multiply. With sigmoid units each local derivative is at most a quarter. Multiply ten of them and the gradient reaching the first layer is almost zero. That is why deep sigmoid networks learned so slowly. Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams showed in nineteen eighty six that one backward pass gives every gradient for about the cost of one forward pass. Without that, training large networks would be impossible. Cognitive load theory says novices drown in symbols. So start with a graph of three nodes and real numbers. Students compute the forward pass, then the backward pass, on paper. Only then generalise. Quick check! The derivative of the loss with respect to a is two, and the derivative of a with respect to w is three. What is the derivative of the loss with respect to w? Six. Two times three. That one multiplication, repeated at every node from the loss backwards, is all backpropagation does. In the app, open the backprop lab. Run one forward pass, then step the gradients backwards node by node and check each multiplication. Your turn. Why does the gradient shrink as it travels back through many sigmoid layers? Because each local derivative is at most a quarter, and they multiply. Remember: backprop is the chain rule on a graph, one backward pass gives every gradient, and small locals vanish. Try it in your next lecture: draw a three-node graph with real numbers on the board. Pairs compute every gradient by hand, then check against the framework's answer.

body.en:
A neural network is a composition of simple differentiable operations, best drawn as a computational graph. The forward pass evaluates each node from inputs to loss and caches intermediate values. Backpropagation then traverses the graph in reverse, multiplying each node’s local derivative by the upstream gradient: ∂L/∂w = ∂L/∂a ⋅ ∂a/∂w. Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams (1986) showed that this yields every partial derivative for roughly the cost of one forward pass, which is what makes training large networks feasible.

Because gradients are products of local derivatives, their size depends on depth. A sigmoid’s derivative is at most 0.25, so after ten layers the gradient can shrink by a factor of a million; this vanishing-gradient problem motivated ReLU activations, careful initialisation, normalisation and residual connections (Goodfellow et al., 2016, ch. 6 and 8).

Students often treat backprop as either magic or as a page of indices. Sweller’s (1988) cognitive load theory suggests why: novices cannot hold notation and concept at once. Worked examples with three nodes and concrete numbers, followed by a gradient check against finite differences, build the concept before the matrix notation.

الشبكة العصبية تركيب من عمليات بسيطة قابلة للاشتقاق، وأفضل ما تُرسم به شبكة حسابية. يحسب المرور الأمامي كل عقدة من المدخلات إلى الخسارة ويحفظ القيم الوسيطة. ثم يجتاز الانتشار العكسي الشبكة بالعكس، ضاربًا المشتقة المحلية لكل عقدة في التدرّج القادم من الأعلى: ∂⁦L/⁩∂⁦w =⁩ ∂⁦L/⁩∂a ⋅ ∂⁦a/⁩∂w. وبيّن Rumelhart وHinton وWilliams (١٩٨٦) أن هذا يعطي كل المشتقات الجزئية بتكلفة تقارب مرورًا أماميًا واحدًا، وهو ما يجعل تدريب الشبكات الكبيرة ممكنًا.

ولأن التدرّجات حواصل ضرب لمشتقات محلية، يعتمد حجمها على العمق. فمشتقة sigmoid لا تتجاوز 0.25، لذا قد يصغر التدرّج بعد عشر طبقات بمعامل مليون، وقد دفعت مشكلة التدرّج المتلاشي هذه إلى دوال ReLU، والتهيئة المدروسة، والتطبيع، والوصلات المتبقية (Goodfellow وآخرون، ٢٠١٦، الفصلان ٦ و٨).

وكثيرًا ما يعامل الطلاب الانتشار العكسي إما سحرًا أو صفحة من الرموز السفلية. وتفسّر نظرية العبء المعرفي عند Sweller (١٩٨٨) السبب: لا يستطيع المبتدئون حمل الرموز والمفهوم معًا. فالأمثلة المحلولة بثلاث عقد وأعداد ملموسة، يتبعها فحص للتدرّج بالفروق المحدودة، تبني المفهوم قبل صيغة المصفوفات.

transcript.en: Take the sentence: the student put the laptop in the bag because it was full. What does it refer to? People answer instantly. Older language models often guessed the laptop. Today: scaled dot-product attention, why it is divided by the square root of d, and how to teach the transformer without drowning students. Attention lets every token build its new representation as a weighted average of all the tokens. The weights say how relevant each other token is. So it can look straight at the bag. Each token makes three vectors. Its query asks what it needs, each key says what a token offers, and values carry the content. Scores are queries times keys, divided by root d, then softmax. Here are one head's attention weights from it to the other nouns. Most of the weight goes to bag. The student and the laptop get little. If query and key entries have variance one, their dot product has variance d. Large scores push softmax into saturation, where gradients vanish. Dividing by root d keeps the variance near one. Vaswani and colleagues' diagram has too much in it for a first lecture. Start with one head, three tokens and two dimensions. Students compute the scores by hand, then you add heads, layers and positions. Quick check! The key dimension d is sixty four. By what number do we divide the raw attention scores? Eight, the square root of sixty four. Without it, scores would have a standard deviation near eight and softmax would almost always pick one token. In the app, open the attention lab. Type a sentence, pick a word, and see which words it attends to. Change the sentence and watch the weights move. Your turn. Attention alone treats its inputs as a set. What does the transformer add so word order matters? Positional encodings. Remember: attention is a weighted average, scores are queries times keys over root d, and position must be added. Try it in your next lecture: give pairs three two-dimensional query and key vectors. They compute the scores, the softmax and the output by hand, then compare with three lines of NumPy.

body.en:
Scaled dot-product attention (Vaswani et al., 2017) lets each token compute its new representation as a weighted average of value vectors, with weights given by softmax(QKᵀ/√d). Queries, keys and values are learned linear projections of the token embeddings. Multi-head attention runs several such maps in parallel so different heads can capture different relations, such as syntax and coreference.

The 1/√d factor is not cosmetic. If the entries of q and k are independent with variance 1, then q⋅k has variance d. Large scores push softmax towards a one-hot output where its gradient is nearly zero, so training stalls; dividing by √d restores unit variance. Because attention is permutation-equivariant, transformers add positional encodings to inject order. Self-attention costs O(n²) in sequence length, which explains context-length limits.

The original architecture diagram overwhelms first-time learners. A sequence that starts with one head on three tokens in two dimensions, computed by hand, then adds the softmax temperature, multiple heads, residual connections, layer norm and position, keeps cognitive load manageable and makes later reading of the paper possible.

transcript.en: Our best team topped the course leaderboard by a wide margin. Then we noticed they had tuned forty models on the test set. Their final score measured their persistence, not their model. Today: how models are evaluated honestly, how to document them, and how to assess machine learning students when they can use language models. Honest evaluation uses three splits. Train fits the weights, validation chooses the model and settings, and test is opened once, at the end. Every peek at test makes its score more optimistic. With one percent positives, a model that always says no is ninety nine percent accurate and useless. Report precision, recall and calibration, and break results down by subgroup. This classifier has ninety one percent recall overall. Split by group, it is ninety four percent for one and seventy two for the other. The average hid the gap. Mitchell and colleagues proposed model cards: a short document with intended use, training data, metrics by subgroup, and known limits. Asking students to write one makes evaluation a habit. Students can generate working code in seconds. So assess what a model cannot do for them. Use oral defences of their own notebooks, require an error analysis on their data, and grade the process. Quick check! A team chose its best model by test score, out of forty. Is that test score an honest estimate of performance on new data? No. Picking the maximum of forty noisy scores selects luck as well as skill. The test set has become a validation set, and they need a fresh one. In the app, open the overfitting lab. Watch validation error as complexity rises, then ask students where they would stop, and why the test set must stay closed. Your turn. Fraud is one transaction in a thousand. A model flags nothing and scores ninety nine point nine percent accuracy. Which metric exposes it? Recall, which is zero. Remember: open the test set once, report metrics by subgroup, write a model card, and assess what language models cannot do for students. Try it this term: add a ten minute oral defence to your next project. Ask each student to explain one error their model makes and one design choice they would change.

body.en:
A model’s reported score is only meaningful if the data behind it played no part in building the model. Use a training set to fit, a validation set or cross-validation to choose architectures and hyperparameters, and a test set opened once. Selecting the best of many models by test score introduces selection bias, the same winner’s curse seen on public leaderboards. Leakage through duplicated records, future information or preprocessing on all the data is the most common error in student projects.

Accuracy hides failure on rare classes and on subgroups. Report precision, recall, calibration and confusion matrices, disaggregated by relevant groups. Mitchell et al. (2019) proposed model cards that document intended use, evaluation data, disaggregated metrics, ethical considerations and caveats; requiring one per project turns evaluation into a habit rather than an afterthought.

Generative models can now write much of a typical ML assignment. Assessment that still measures learning targets what a tool cannot do on the student’s behalf: oral defences of their own notebook, error analysis on data they collected, design rationales, and graded process artefacts such as experiment logs. Be explicit about permitted tool use, and align tasks with outcomes as Biggs and Tang recommend.
body.ar:
لا تكون درجة النموذج المعلنة ذات معنى إلا إذا لم يكن للبيانات التي وراءها أي دور في بناء النموذج. استخدم مجموعة تدريب للتركيب، ومجموعة تحقق أو تحققًا متقاطعًا لاختيار البنى والمعاملات الفائقة، ومجموعة اختبار تُفتح مرة واحدة. واختيار الأفضل من نماذج كثيرة بدرجة الاختبار يُدخل تحيّز الاختيار، وهي لعنة الفائز ذاتها التي تُرى في لوحات الترتيب العامة. والتسريب عبر السجلات المكررة أو معلومات المستقبل أو المعالجة على كل البيانات هو أكثر الأخطاء شيوعًا في مشاريع الطلاب.

وتخفي الدقة الإخفاق في الفئات النادرة والمجموعات الفرعية. فاذكر الدقة الإيجابية والاستدعاء والمعايرة ومصفوفات الالتباس، مفصّلة حسب المجموعات ذات الصلة. واقترحت Mitchell وزملاؤها (٢٠١٩) بطاقات النموذج التي توثّق الاستخدام المقصود، وبيانات التقييم، والمقاييس المفصّلة، والاعتبارات الأخلاقية، والتحفظات، واشتراط بطاقة لكل مشروع يجعل التقييم عادة لا فكرة لاحقة.

وتستطيع النماذج التوليدية الآن كتابة جزء كبير من تكليف معتاد في تعلّم الآلة. والتقييم الذي يظل يقيس التعلّم يستهدف ما لا تستطيع الأداة فعله نيابة عن الطالب: الدفاع الشفوي عن دفتره البرمجي، وتحليل الأخطاء على بيانات جمعها، ومبررات التصميم، ومخرجات العملية المقيّمة كسجلات التجارب. وكن صريحًا بشأن الاستخدام المسموح للأدوات، ونسّق المهام مع النواتج كما يوصي Biggs وTang.
